question: An engineer asked your developer productivity agent to add rate limiting to a legacy API gateway, a domain that the engineer had never worked in. The agent implemented it from a short prose request, and all tests passed. In production, the shared counter store went down, and the gateway rejected every request. The engineer had never considered this case. Which change to the workflow would most likely have surfaced this case before implementation?

options.text: Before implementing, have the agent ask the engineer questions about design considerations, such as gateway behavior when the counter store is unavailable.
options.reason: In an unfamiliar domain, the interview pattern has Claude ask questions before implementing. These questions surface considerations that the developer did not anticipate, such as failure modes.

options.text: Before implementing, write a test suite that covers the expected limits and the edge cases that the engineer can list, and then iterate by sharing each test failure with the agent.
options.reason: Test-driven iteration checks the behavior that the tests describe. The engineer never considered the counter store outage, so no test would cover it, and the tests would not surface it.

options.text: After implementing, collect all of the code review findings and send them to the agent in one detailed message so that it fixes all of them together.
options.reason: A single detailed message is the way to fix interacting issues in existing code. It acts only after implementation and does not surface unanticipated design considerations beforehand.

options.text: Before implementing, give the agent two or three concrete examples of request counts with the expected allow or reject decision for each count.
options.reason: Input/output examples clarify a transformation that prose descriptions leave inconsistent. These examples only show cases that the engineer already anticipated, so they would not reveal the counter store outage.
